opportunity.title: Towards a Global South-Driven Future for Development Studies
opportunity.host: Global Development Institute, University of Manchester
opportunity.theme: Decolonizing development studies through Global South perspectives
opportunity.description: Two international workshops for early-career researchers (PhD awarded after October 1, 2017, or currently enrolled in a PhD) based in Asia and Africa to centre voices on the future of development studies. The first workshop will be held in Bandung, Indonesia in April 2027, hosted by Padjadjaran University. Participants will present extended abstracts (750–1,000 words) on four themes: framing development, the scope of development studies, decolonization of knowledge, or emerging topics reshaping the field. Accepted papers will be revised into short papers (3,000–4,000 words) or full papers (6,000–8,000 words) for publication in an edited collection with a prestigious academic press or as a special issue in a leading development studies journal. The workshop includes three days: participant presentations, feedback on Indonesia-based early-career work, and professional development sessions (article writing, journal selection, grants, career opportunities). Funded by British Academy Writing Workshop grant (IWW25/100268); covers return flights from within Asia and three nights' accommodation.

opportunity.title: Caste, Corporeality, and Performance
opportunity.theme: Caste, corporeality, and performance; the intersection of caste studies with performance and embodiment
opportunity.description: A special issue of the peer-reviewed, open-access journal GPS: Global Performance Studies, examining how caste is performed, reproduced, and resisted through the body. The issue brings together the study of caste with performance and corporeality studies, exploring choreographic logics of caste, embodied caste ideology, and how performance might offer resistance or liberation from caste systems. Guest editors: Anusha Kedhar (UC Riverside) and Brahma Prakash (Jawaharlal Nehru University). Submissions may take multiple forms including academic articles (6,000–9,000 words), performance recordings, creative writing, photography, interviews, and other artistic works with critical reflection.

opportunity.theme: South Asian futures, imaginaries, and emplacement in the early modern period to present
opportunity.description: A two-and-a-half-day advanced dissertation workshop for doctoral candidates who have completed research and are writing dissertations. Ten participants will work with mentors Sangeeta Banerji, Tarini Bedi, and Lisa Björkman in Shanghai, with one preliminary virtual meeting. Participants present work for peer feedback in seminar format. The workshop explores how people in South Asia imagine and articulate future possibilities through projects, practices, and modes of emplacement, situating these within wider Asian processes. Disciplines across social sciences and humanities welcome; special invitation to performance studies, literary studies, anthropology, history of migration, religion, and media.
